# 📝 Documentation Change Review

## Metadata

- Document path(s):
- Author:
- Reviewer:
- Related issue / PR:
- Commit:
- Date:
- Audience:

## Purpose and source of truth

Explain who needs the documentation and what task it supports. Identify source files, package scripts, workflow definitions, or confirmed external references used to validate claims.

## Change summary

- [ ] New page or guide
- [ ] Correction to existing behavior
- [ ] Setup / usage update
- [ ] Architecture or diagram update
- [ ] Security / privacy clarification
- [ ] Examples / visual assets
- [ ] Navigation / documentation index
- [ ] Template or governance update

## Accuracy review

- [ ] File paths exist.
- [ ] Commands match package scripts.
- [ ] Dependency and runtime versions are verified.
- [ ] Current and proposed behavior are clearly separated.
- [ ] No unsupported API, AI, persistence, or deployment feature is claimed.
- [ ] Examples use synthetic data.
- [ ] Images are described and are not mislabelled as screenshots.
- [ ] Third-party material is credited where required.

## Accessibility and maintainability

- [ ] Headings are hierarchical.
- [ ] Links have descriptive text.
- [ ] Tables are readable.
- [ ] Code fences specify a language.
- [ ] Images have useful alternative text.
- [ ] The docs index and related links are updated.

## Validation

- [ ] Internal Markdown links resolve.
- [ ] Referenced commands were run or labelled as unverified.
- [ ] Mermaid syntax was reviewed.
- [ ] Readability was checked at normal scale.

## Decision

Reviewer, accepted corrections, unresolved gaps, owner, and follow-up date:
